page: UpCloud STARTER-1xCPU-1GB is an entry-level virtual server instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is configured with a single shared vCPU running on an AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, 1.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 10 GB SSD for local storage. The CPU features 64 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for vector and cryptographic instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, SHA-NI, and VAES. Each deployment includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without bundled GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results reflect the instance's single-core execution strengths and multi-core resource limits. The modern AMD architecture demonstrates exceptional single-core processing in stress-ng with a score of 3,832.77, placing it in the top 10 percent of single-thread benchmarks. Single-threaded data compression also ranks high, producing 32.66 GB/sec in gzip testing. Conversely, because the instance relies on a single shared core and 1.0 GB of RAM, throughput-heavy benchmarks such as PassMark overall CPU (3,428.38), multi-core stress-ng, uncached read memory bandwidth (35.83 GB/sec), and static web serving (5.4 GB/sec) score in the lower percentiles.

The primary tradeoff of the instance stems from its shared single-vCPU architecture and 1.0 GB memory capacity, which precludes parallel processing and memory-intensive applications. However, with its modern AMD EPYC foundation and low entry-tier footprint, it provides cost-efficient baseline compute for lightweight utility tasks, development sandboxes, basic automated scripts, and minimal microservices.
description: UpCloud STARTER-1xCPU-1GB is an entry-level virtual server designed for lightweight computing tasks. Powered by the KVM hypervisor, it features 1 shared vCPU from an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz, 1.0 GB of memory, and 10 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Instruction support includes modern extensions such as AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and VAES. While overall throughput is constrained by the single shared core and small memory pool, resulting in modest PassMark and aggregate multi-core scores, the architecture delivers top-tier single-core execution in stress-ng and strong single-threaded gzip compression at 32.66 GB/sec. Accompanied by a single public IPv4 address, the instance offers an economical solution for low-traffic services, test environments, background utility scripts, and entry-level automation.
